abstract: Define $$ P(y)= \frac{\lfloor y\rfloor(\lfloor y\rfloor+1)}{y^3} \{y\}(1-\{y\}),\qquad y\ge1, $$ and $$ T(x)=\sum_{a,b\le\sqrt x}\mu(a)\mu(b)P\!\left(\frac{x}{ab}\right). $$ The Riemann hypothesis is equivalent both to $$ T(x)\ll_\varepsilon x^{1/2+\varepsilon} $$ for every $\varepsilon>0$, and to the corresponding dyadic mean-square bound. The reduction rests on an exact truncation identity for $\mu$ already stated by Helfgott and Thompson (the case $K=2$ of Heath-Brown's identity), applied with a weight whose periodization is the kernel $P$; the new content is this explicit positive kernel, its spectral structure, and the detector certificates. The kernel is entrywise nonnegative and contains no asymptotic remainder. It is nevertheless highly indefinite: along square primorials both inertias grow at least as $\log x/\log\log x$, while on a specific squarefree primorial star the centered kernel has exact inertia $(1,m-2,0)$ and, by interlacing, the negative inertia on the full squarefree support is unbounded. We construct minimal degree-six, degree-nine, and degree-twelve nonnegative detectors which remove respectively the first one, two, and three odd collective residues. We also give a degree-fifteen detector, minimal in the same endpoint-flat polynomial class, which removes the first four odd collective residues; its positivity is certified by an exact shifted Faulhaber--Bernstein expansion. An analogous degree-eighteen certificate removes the first five odd residues. These are equivalent criteria and structural results, not a proof of RH.
author: lihongmin
change_summary:
1. Degree-fifteen minimality paragraph (Section 8, after (8.17)), per the v2 review: 'the remaining degree-at-most-fourteen quotient' is replaced by 'If deg V<=14, the quotient by u^2(1-u)^9 has degree at most three, and its four coefficients are killed by the three remaining odd-coefficient conditions and zero mean', stating the dimension of the four-condition linear system explicitly. No mathematical content changed.
2. Section 8, per the review of the previous revision attempt: the five separate minimality arguments are replaced by Proposition 8.1, stated for 1<=l<=5 and now explicitly attributed to sylve_recursions, rStation paper 44 v2, Theorem 2.1 (new reference [8]), which proves the bound for every l and whose denominator (1.2)-(1.3) is that of (8.0b); the uniform proof is identified as the argument of [8], reproduced for completeness, while the five finite minimality results are recorded as first obtained in this paper. The endpoint-lemma sentence is reconciled (the lemma and bound hold for all l>=1; the proposition is stated at the five constructed levels). Introduction, Section 9 and Section 10 contribution statements adjusted accordingly.
3. Section 8 closing paragraph: 'conjectural continuation to every residue level' replaced by an acknowledgement that all-level positivity is proved in bramble_trace, rStation paper 46 v2, Theorem 1 (new reference [9]), which is not used here.
4. Section 6: Corollary 6.1 (Cauchy interlacing) gives negative inertia at least m-2 on the full squarefree support; Section 10 rewritten accordingly.
5. Section 4: Corollary 4.1 (critical endpoint): T(x) is not o(x^{1/2}), the weighted L^2 integral diverges, and T=O(x^{1/2}) implies RH with simple zeros; stated as an application of classical arguments, not as new.
6. Introduction: theorem locators added for [3] (Thm 1.3(a),(b)) and [4] (Thms 3.1, 4.1; Lemma 9.1, Prop. 9.2), checked against the cited arXiv versions; dated literature-check records removed; reference [7] updated to the published version (Res. Number Theory 9 (2023), art. 6).
7. Introduction: Baez-Duarte locator completed against arXiv:math/0504402v1: Theorem 3.1 (RH convolution criterion), operator G_phi defined in (3.1), equivalence (3.14). No mathematical content changed.
8. Corollary 4.1: 'in the spirit of [2]' replaced by exact locators Proposition 4.1, Theorem 4.2 (4.3), Theorem 4.1 of [2], checked against arXiv:math/0504402v1; proof unchanged and independent of [2].
title: A Positive Reciprocal-Product Criterion for the Riemann Hypothesis
